description: 164 is not a number highlighted in the Bible or in classical Jewish numerology (gematria) with any specific symbolic role. Interpretations can be constructed by breaking it down into components (for example, 4 × 41, or the sum of other numbers), but none of these carry traditional authority. The number does not appear directly in any central biblical text and has no known symbolic value in Jewish or Christian tradition.

versions.meaning: The number 164 has no well-established or known symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.

versions.reason: [major] The description mentions the year 164 BC and the Maccabees’ rededication of the temple as a historical link. This is an interesting and relevant detail, but it disrupts the flow of a text that otherwise argues the number has no symbolic meaning. This information would fit better as a footnote.; [minor] The cited Bible verse (Rev 21:17) mentions 144, not 164. Therefore, it is not appropriate to bring it in, and it is correct that it is not referenced in the description. However, care should be taken to ensure the description does not give the impression that the number never appears in any biblical context without addressing this point.; [minor] The meaning field is somewhat long and could have been more concise. A shorter phrasing such as "No established biblical symbolism" would have been more consistent with a meaning field.

footnotes.text: Historically, the year 164 BC can be linked to the Maccabees' rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem after its desecration by Antiochus IV Epiphanes. This event is celebrated through the festival of Hanukkah (see 1 Macc 4:36–59). Although the year itself is historically significant, the number 164 is not attributed any symbolic value in Jewish or Christian tradition.
